next_steps: Run 10% canary with v1.2 (quantized) for 48 hours starting 2025-06-20
Redwood SE to share runbook draft and rollback playbook link by 2025-06-20
Customer SRE (Marcus) to enable token-level cost telemetry in staging by 2025-06-22
Schedule dry-run cutover (no traffic) with infra team 2025-06-24
action_items: Samir Patel - send updated pricing for dedicated + canary overage - due 2025-06-20
Lena Gómez - publish prelaunch runbook (Google Doc link) and canary gating checklist - due 2025-06-20
Marcus Lee - flip on enhanced tracing & forward spans to Redwood tracing endpoint in staging - due 2025-06-22

summary: Weekly POC sync focused on go-live planning: finalize canary percentage, gating metrics, telemetry needs, runbook ownership, and dry-run scheduling. Team aligned on 10% canary for v1.2 quantized model; Redwood to deliver runbook and pricing; MiraData to prepare tracing and on-call rosters.
topics: Gating metrics (p99 latency, error rate, model quality regressions)
Security/compliance handoff and private deployment questions
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-18 14:00 PT | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Alicia (CSM), Jenna (MiraData Product), Marcus (MiraData SRE), Priya (Eng Mgr), Tomás (Sec Arch)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call — trying to keep this tight, we've got a 45 to 55 minute window. the goal today is to lock canary percent, telemetry gating, and owners on the runbook so we can start a dry run next week.

[00:18] Jenna: yep, sounds good. i want to make sure we also cover any data residency or KMS questions prior to cutover, last time that popped up.

[00:28] Marcus: and from SRE we need tracing and token-cost visibility; without that we can't estimate monthly spend for the pilot.

[00:36] Lena: quick context — the POC workload in staging has been stable, we've exercised kv cache warm-up and the quantized v1.2 build runs ~2.1x cost reduction on our internal micro-benchmarks, p99 latencies are around 180-220ms with the current batch config. those numbers are with 8k context and the prefix cache enabled.

[01:05] Priya: is that with the continuous batching you mentioned? last sync you said batching hurts tail at high concurrency.

[01:12] Lena: yeah, we tuned the batching policy to prefer low-latency SLOs; it favors smaller batches under 20ms enqueue threshold which keeps p99 where you saw. if you push concurrency to 600 concurrent requests it will back up and p99 will shift — but our canary will start at low traffic (10%).

[01:34] Alicia: just to confirm the plan from last week — we try canary 10% traffic for 48 hours, collect telemetry, then promote if no gating violations. is that still the desired cadence?

[01:45] Jenna: 10% feels right. i'd rather start small and ramp than risk customer impact. what's the gating surface again?

[01:51] Samir: gating metrics we propose: 
- p99 latency increase >20% over baseline for more than 15m,
- error rate spike >0.5% absolute,
- quality regressions: measured via our prompt set evals -- if top-line exact match / RMSE falls beyond threshold, auto-fail,
- cost variance: token-level cost > +30% relative to baseline for sustained 2 hours.

[02:20] Tomás: quick security note — for private deployment customers want KMS-managed keys; is that available on the dedicated plan or only private? last doc i saw referenced HSM integrations but not for dedicated.

[02:33] Samir: dedicated supports customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; HSM integration for private is on roadmap but we can provide SOC2 artifacts and key rotation policies now. i'll send the snapshot after the call.

[02:44] Marcus: on the telemetry side we need token-level cost per request and per-route latency percentiles. can Redwood emit OpenTelemetry spans to our collector?

[02:52] Lena: yes, we can forward OTLP spans to your collector. there's a small sampling config and we recommend full tracing for the canary window, then sample down to 10% in prod to control volume. we'll include exporter config in the runbook.

[03:12] Jenna: can you also include a list of dashboards and alert thresholds so our on-call knows what to watch?

[03:18] Lena: absolutely — Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules will be in the runbook doc.

[03:24] [--- 7m omitted: brief sync on perf numbers, load generator config, and tokenization differences. audio glitch at 00:10:42; transcript may skip small bits ---]

[10:30] Samir: returning — re: rollback plan, Lena can you outline the automated rollback triggers?

[10:37] Lena: the runtime supports policy-based routing; for canary we'll set traffic weights 90/10. if any gating metric triggers, the controller will immediately shift 100% back to baseline model and signal an alert. that is automated; manual rollback is also a button in the console. we'll capture the call-flow and who clicks what in the runbook.

[10:58] Priya: ok, who is responsible for the actual click? SRE or Redwood? we need to be explicit so our pager duty knows.

[11:06] Samir: good point. proposed: initial auto-rollback from system — event goes to on-call (Marcus) and to Redwood SE (Lena). manual rollback requires confirmation from customer SRE within 10 minutes; otherwise system stays rolled back. we'll put exact escalation steps in doc.

[11:28] Marcus: that works. also we need a dry-run where we simulate a roll forward and rollback without traffic so playbooks are practiced.

[11:36] Alicia: let's schedule the dry-run on 2025-06-24 as a calendar hold — Samir can you propose times?

[11:43] Samir: will do.

[11:46] Jenna: about A/B vs canary, is it possible to run a small A/B for quality comparisons? we'd like to compare v1.1 baseline against v1.2 on a held set of 5k prompts.

[11:58] Lena: yes — we can do A/B evaluation using request tagging and capture historical hits. two options: traffic A/B (real user traffic split) or shadow testing where v1.2 runs in parallel and logs outputs for offline evals. recommended: do shadow + small A/B 5% for initial quality metrics.

[12:23] Tomás: any PII concerns in shadowing? we might need to mask or redact before logging for offline evals.

[12:30] Samir: agreed. we support configurable redaction rules and can redact tokens or drop full transcripts before shipping to your eval pipeline. we'll include standard redaction patterns.

[12:45] [16:00–26:00 condensed: discussion about redaction patterns, token sampling, and eval harness setup. Lena to share eval harness link and scripts.]

[26:12] Lena: on instrumentation — for token-level cost we attach metadata to each response, you get tokens_in, tokens_out, and estimated cost field. for heavy workloads consider enabling prefix cache so repeated prompts cost less.

[26:30] Marcus: prefix cache seems helpful but does it change determinism for A/B tests? we want apples-to-apples.

[26:38] Lena: good catch — prefix cache can change latencies but not model outputs for identical requests; however cache warm-up behavior can create different perf profiles. for A/B quality runs, disable prefix cache or ensure both sides have same cache state. we'll mention that in the runbook.

[26:55] Samir: okay, timeline recap:
- 2025-06-20: start 10% canary for 48 hours with full tracing and shadow logging,
- 2025-06-22: telemetry review and decision point for ramp,
- 2025-06-24: dry-run cutover (no traffic),
- 2025-06-25: potential ramp to 50% if no gating issues.

[27:28] Priya: who signs off for the ramp? product or infra?

[27:33] Jenna: product owns quality signoff, infra owns ops signoff. both need to approve in the doc.

[27:40] Samir: we'll add a signoff matrix in the runbook with explicit names and backup approvers.

[27:47] [minor cross-talk]

[28:02] Tomás: on compliance handoff — you mentioned SOC2 artifacts. can you send the latest attestation and pen test summary? security will need that for our procurement packet.

[28:13] Samir: yes, i'll attach SOC2, ISO summary, and the recent pentest redacted report. expect links by EOD.

[28:20] Marcus: also need retention policy details for logs and spans; our legal wants 90-day retention max for pilot.

[28:27] Lena: retention is configurable per-route; we'll add configuration examples showing 30/90/365 day policies and retention lifecycle steps.

[28:36] Jenna: pricing question — if the canary runs over the reserved capacity, what happens? we have a committed Dedicated pool but might spike.

[28:45] Samir: you'll get overage billing at reduced rate for canary bursts — I'll include a canary overage table in pricing doc, and a suggestion to buy short-term burst credits if you expect heavy spikes during tests.

[28:58] Priya: fine. please include a worked example for our expected call-volume.

[29:04] Samir: will do.

[29:10] [--- 10m omitted: detailed walkthrough of runbook sections, who writes what, pointer to shared Google Doc (link removed in transcript) ---]

[40:30] Alicia: quick note on SLOs — we should add an error budget burn-rate alert that we can correlate to product metrics.

[40:38] Lena: yes, we'll add burn-rate alerts and a toggle to pause batching to reduce tail. we'll document the tradeoffs.

[40:50] Marcus: for the dry-run can we also exercise failure modes: network partition, model oom, and slow disk I/O? we want to validate fallback to regional replica.

[40:59] Samir: absolutely — dry-run will have a failure-mode checklist; we'll simulate region failover and validate auto-fallback to the second region.

[41:10] Jenna: okay, anything else?

[41:13] Priya: i think that's it. i want to emphasize the human ops checklist — names, phone numbers, eskalation.

[41:21] Samir: noted. i'll make sure runbook has pager roster, escalation windows, and contact matrix.

[41:28] Alicia: last item — scheduling: Samir to send calendar invites for dry-run and for the 48-hour canary start time.

[41:35] Samir: will send invites and the runbook link.

[41:40] Jenna: thanks all.

[41:42] [meet close]
